saints.name: St. Helena
saints.title: Empress and Mother of Constantine
saints.shortBlurb: The mother of Constantine the Great, honored by tradition as the finder of the True Cross…
biography: Helena, born of humble origins about the middle of the third century, was the mother of Constantine the Great, and when her son gained the empire she was honored with the title of Augusta. Already advanced in years, she embraced the Christian faith with fervor and used her position for works of charity and church-building.

About 326 she made a celebrated pilgrimage to the Holy Land, where tradition credits her with the discovery of the True Cross of Christ and with raising churches at the holy places, including Bethlehem and the Mount of Olives. She died about 330, revered ever since as a model of piety and generosity.
saints.knownFor: Her pilgrimage and the tradition of finding the True Cross.
